Hartside Pass: England's Magnificent A-Road Climb

The A686 from Penrith to Alston is one of England's finest motorcycle roads. Climbing to 580 metres at Hartside Top, it offers sweeping bends, panoramic views, and a sense of scale that's rare in England. The road follows an ancient route across the North Pennines and rewards riders with one of the best views in the country from its summit.

The Ascent

From Penrith, the A686 heads east across the Eden Valley floor before beginning its climb. The initial section through Langwathby is gentle, but once you leave Melmerby, the road steepens dramatically. The next five miles climb relentlessly, with long, sweeping bends that open up extraordinary views behind you — the Lake District fells appear on the western horizon, and on clear days, you can see the Solway Firth and Scotland beyond.

Hartside Top

The summit at Hartside Top (580m) was once home to the legendary Hartside Top Cafe — a mecca for motorcyclists across northern England. The cafe unfortunately burnt down in 2019 and its future remains uncertain. Even without the cafe, the summit viewpoint is worth a stop. The panorama extends across the Eden Valley to the Lake District, Scottish Borders, and Yorkshire Dales on clear days.

Hartside is England's answer to an Alpine pass. The scale of the views, the length of the climb, and the quality of the bends make it a genuine world-class motorcycle road.

The Descent to Alston

From the summit, the road descends through increasingly wild country to Alston — England's highest market town at 300 metres. The descent is faster than the ascent, with long straights across exposed moorland. Alston itself is worth exploring — a steep main street with local shops and tea rooms, and the narrow-gauge South Tynedale Railway.

The Full Route

The best way to enjoy Hartside is as part of a circular route. From Penrith, ride the A686 east to Alston, then take the A689 north to Brampton. Head west on the minor roads through the Eden Valley back to Penrith. This 70-mile loop covers varied terrain and takes about 2.5 hours with stops.

Practical Information

  • Distance: 22 miles from Penrith to Alston
  • Summit height: 580 metres (1,903 feet)
  • Fuel: Fill up in Penrith — Alston has one fuel station with limited hours
  • Surface: Good tarmac throughout, well-maintained A-road
  • Winter: Can be closed in snow. Ice is common October-March
  • Best conditions: Clear days for the views, but atmospheric in low cloud
keyTakeaways: The A686 from Penrith to Alston is 22 miles of one of England's finest A-road climbs.
Hartside Top reaches 580 metres, with views across the Eden Valley to the Lake District, Borders and Dales.
The legendary Hartside Top Cafe burnt down in 2019, but the summit viewpoint is still worth a stop.
Alston is England's highest market town at 300 metres, home to the narrow-gauge South Tynedale Railway.
Enjoy it as a 70-mile loop via the A689 to Brampton; fill up in Penrith as Alston's fuel has limited hours.

faq.a: Hartside Top reaches 580 metres, making the A686 one of England's highest A-roads. On clear days the panorama extends across the Eden Valley to the Lake District fells, the Scottish Borders and the Yorkshire Dales. The scale of the views, length of climb and quality of the bends make it a world-class road.

faq.q: Is the Hartside Top Cafe still open?
faq.a: No. The legendary Hartside Top Cafe, long a mecca for motorcyclists across northern England, burnt down in 2019 and its future remains uncertain. Even without the cafe, the summit viewpoint at 580 metres is well worth a stop for the extraordinary views in every direction on a clear day.

faq.q: Where should I fuel up for the A686?
faq.a: Fill up in Penrith before you start, as Alston has just one fuel station with limited hours. The 22-mile road from Penrith to Alston has good tarmac throughout, but it can be closed in snow and ice is common from October to March, so check conditions in the colder months.

faq.q: What is the best way to enjoy Hartside?
faq.a: Ride it as part of a circular route. From Penrith take the A686 east to Alston, then the A689 north to Brampton, returning west on minor roads through the Eden Valley to Penrith. This 70-mile loop covers varied terrain and takes about 2.5 hours with stops, including time to explore Alston.
